name: session-watch-v1
scope: Synthetic fixed-wire contract; a fixture is not a test result or real device/network validation.

source.verification: events/response/subscriptions blobs identical between both fixed commits; release stream_subscriptions ACK, batch and events_lost handling inspected separately.

rules: Subscribe global lifecycle, wait for ACK, read snapshot; rebuild subscription with per-pane status entries, wait for ACK, then snapshot again.
Lifecycle push event names use snake_case; pane-specific agent status push uses pane.agent_status_changed.
Events are invalidations only. At most one snapshot in flight and a coalesced dirty counter; never apply payloads to cache.
An event during a read schedules another read; snapshot and events have no shared remote sequence.
On events_lost, EOF, invalid data or subscription failure, publish stale before channel retirement; await old channel cleanup before replacement.
A missing event method is unavailable with an authoritative one-shot snapshot; it does not imply SSH or terminal disconnection.
Publication is fenced by connection generation in the caller and observation epoch plus local revision. Terminal full/delta cannot change board freshness.
Pause retires the epoch subscription and observer while retaining SSH; explicit resume re-subscribes and obtains snapshot plus terminal full.
User selection carries pane_id and terminal_id from the reviewed row. Re-check both against the latest authoritative snapshot; never substitute a newer same-name pane.
Watching issues only events.subscribe/session.snapshot; it cannot send input, prompt, resize, takeover or PTY requests.

cases.scenario: ACK precedes authoritative initial snapshot; no fresh state before reconciliation
Pane added/closed/exited and status changes trigger current snapshot metadata
Event payload contradicts snapshot; only snapshot wins
events_lost while snapshot in flight marks stale immediately; old read cannot freshen loss
Subscription EOF retries on same SSH with ACK before snapshot
Storm coalesces without a payload backlog or concurrent snapshots
Paused epoch and late old events cannot update new epoch
Active terminal replaced/removed ends original observer; never reselects
New row can be selected by exact typed intent; reused old row rejected
Unsupported subscribe keeps one-shot observe available and board unavailable
Read-only watch traffic contains zero input and resize requests
